the command and CI output own its current result</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="process-note">Process Note</h2> <p>The machinery exists to protect measurement claims from unchecked summaries, stale assumptions, and review-induced drift.</p> <p>This project is developed by a human researcher directing a multi-agent AI system he designed and iteratively engineered over the course of the project — the orchestration itself is a second, deliberate piece of engineering alongside the measurement harness and its benchmark, and by now it is interesting in its own right.</p> <p>The full description lives in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> (the loop, the roles, the artifact system, and how the topology itself evolved under its own review machinery); this section is the summary.</p> <p><strong>The division of labor.</strong> Ed sets the research direction, the methodology standards (the decision log&#39;s non-negotiables: raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy headlines, named measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), the hardware and access decisions, and — the part that is easy to underrate — the <em>process policy</em>: every rule below exists because he observed a failure or an opportunity and issued a standing instruction. The AI staff executes: the designated lead agent is the final reviewer and single point of accountability: decomposition, design adjudication, every final diff gate, live verification, merges, and bookkeeping. Independent implementation and review agents do the volume work against pinned specs, adversarial review lenses, test writing, and fresh-instance test auditing; specialist agents handle bounded sweeps. Cross-model review is load-bearing by design: the attributed catch record shows the models and review layers catching different classes of defect.</p> <p><strong>The machinery, briefly.</strong> Independent tasks run as parallel git worktrees, the lead driving each stream&#39;s implementation/review pipeline directly (a topology that is itself the product of a signed cross-model meta-review, then validated by a full session with zero coordination stalls — the evolution is traced in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code>). Every implementation passes through a layered pipeline: a design argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before coding), fresh-instance counterreview lenses with lead-triaged dispositions, a test-amplification round, a writer-never-reviews-its-own-tests audit, the lead&#39;s diff gate, and lead-side live verification on real hardware — the one layer never delegated, because it has repeatedly caught blockers whose own tests were green (the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code). Merges add their own gate: a pre-merge oversight pass by fresh reviewers with distinct angles, and a standing <em>final-head rule</em> — any commit landing after the last review round gets one more fresh review before merge (its first application caught a crash path in a &quot;trivial&quot; late fix). After parallel streams merge, a dedicated integration review hunts the cross-stream defects no per-stream review can see (two interaction defects on its first outing, two more on its second). An event-driven review council convenes for contract-bearing work, and — per Ed&#39;s instruction — its <em>deliberations</em> are recorded, not just its verdicts: the council log preserves positions, the reasoning exchanged, who prevailed and why, and overridden dissents, so a future reader (or model) can reconstruct why any decision was made.</p> <p><strong>The paper trail (each claim traceable to its evidence home; the external re-reduction demonstration is still pending).</strong> Each fact has one home: <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> — the binding design decisions (the log is the count authority), most recording alternatives considered and revisit conditions; <code>docs/council_log.md</code> — the deliberation record; <code>docs/stream_logs/</code> — per-stream decision ledgers committed <em>with</em> the code they justify (wrong decisions are superseded in place, never erased); <code>docs/run_reports/</code> — one record per session with verification evidence, a per-review-layer catch table, and a delegation-calibration ledger (outcomes assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-reported; prompt-defects separated from model-defects). The whole loop is self-instrumenting: every review layer&#39;s unique catches are attributed and tallied, and a layer that stops earning its keep is dropped by its own evidence rule (one already has been). Delegation boundaries move on calibration evidence, not intuition. Lessons are folded into the process playbooks the same session they are learned — measurably: one failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, and zero times after. The loop even reviews itself: a meta-review consensus (C-009) redesigned the coordination topology, and the next session (C-010) validated the redesign with a zero-stall run.</p> <p><strong>What one day of this looks like (2026-07-07).</strong> Five implementation streams plus a repo-wide test audit ran concurrently: statistical uncertainty, contamination detection, deep DVFS telemetry, campaign automation, and a KV-cache size model. All five merged the same day; the test suite grew 254 → 369; the layered review recorded thirteen attributed catches including three blockers that no single reviewer would plausibly have found together. One blocker surfaced only when the real CLI was run against code whose own tests were green, because the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.</p> <p><strong>How the scope grew.</strong> The project began as an architecture sketch for &quot;measure LLM inference energy on edge hardware.&quot; Contracts-first engineering turned that into an auditable instrument: typed configs, self-contained evidence bundles, a strict re-reduction validator. The mock vertical slice proved the math without hardware; the Mac slice produced the first real joules; the flagship run put a 122-billion- parameter mixture-of-experts model through the identical harness and yielded the first real cross-model observation: two confounded points that differ in size, architecture, and quantization, with energy/token behavior consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal model while decode power stays nearly flat — the big model costs time, not watts. This week the instrument gained the statistical and forensic machinery above, and a steelmanned, devil&#39;s-advocated research agenda of 31 tiered questions — 16 answerable on the current hardware alone (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The pattern throughout: capability first, claims only when the instrument can defend them.</p> <p><strong>And the most recent day (2026-07-07/08).</strong> Four checkpointed streams were resumed, completed, and merged in one session: the integrity/ provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed; strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence), the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded ~30 attributed catches, including two blockers no implementer&#39;s tests could see (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation input; a validation-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire contracts overturned by review before they could ever touch hardware, and one fabricated-evidence defect caught only at the lead&#39;s diff gate. The suite went 415 → 546 tests with zero expected failures, and the lead never wrote implementation code and never skipped a gate.</p> <p><strong>Where to look.</strong> <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> is the process description. <code>docs/council_log.md</code> is the deliberation record — C-006 is a full orchestration trace of the five-stream day; C-009/C-010 are the topology meta-review and its validation; C-011 is the critique counter-review. <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> holds the binding design decisions with alternatives considered (the log is the count authority). <code>docs/run_reports/</code> narrates each working session, with per-layer catch tables and the delegation-calibration ledger. The executable orchestration playbooks live outside this repository as reusable skills (council, delegation, multi-stream worktrees, adversarial review, and a top-level operation-loop that sequences them), so the machinery survives this project and transfers to the next one.</p> <h2 id="maintenance-of-this-document">Maintenance Of This Document</h2> <p>Updated at phase transitions and whenever advisor-visible state changes (a gate closes, a verdict lands, the schedule moves). Volatile work-selection facts stay in the state kernel, verification results stay in command/CI output, and decision structure stays in the checked decision-log index. A front-facing change also refreshes <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code>; Ed alone regenerates and deploys the site (D-068).</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>PROJECT_STATUS.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
.codex-bridge/20260807T162728Z-33053-new.log:5629:docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \
.codex-bridge/20260807T162728Z-33053-new.log:5644:docs/site/claims_ladder.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>Claims Ladder - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#global-rules">Global Rules</a> <a href="#ladder">Ladder</a> <a href="#downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-contracts-claims-ladder-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Claims Ladder</h1> <p>Status: binding for reader-facing claims from Slice 2M onward. Decision D-037 records adoption. Per-claim IDs and mechanical enforcement arrive with the Phase 4 claims index; until then, authors apply this ladder during review.</p> <p>This contract governs wording in reports, slides, README/status prose, figure captions, and tables that a reader could treat as a result. Dated run reports, stream logs, council logs, and decision logs may preserve historical wording, but later reader-facing summaries must use the current level.</p> <p>The warning-only prose scan mechanically enumerates <code>README.md</code>, <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>docs/report_src/**</code>, the generated Phase-4 claims projection, Markdown tables/captions under analysis and figure artifacts, and present or future <code>slides/</code>, <code>captions/</code>, and <code>tables/</code> publication trees. Historical <code>docs/run_reports/**</code> records and the decision/council/stream logs are deliberately outside that scan. Warning-only exit behavior remains the D-059 policy: these findings require editorial review but are not structural claim-gate failures.</p> <p>The canonical JSONL accepts two authority-distinct row dialects through one fail-closed validator: the single pre-P2-037 legacy L1 row only under its exact hash-pinned identity, and current rows linked to a governed <code>joulewise.claim_verdicts.v1</code> artifact. Rows with unknown authority fields or a mixture of legacy and engine-linked authority fields are invalid. Verdict semantics belong to <code>joulewise.analysis_engine</code>; the claims-index layer adds only linkage, canonical ordering/rendering, relative-path, editorial, and current production-admission checks. <code>two_look_alpha_spending</code> remains outside claims-index production admission until separately ruled in; current admission is deliberately <code>fixed_n</code> only.</p> <h2 id="global-rules">Global Rules</h2> <ul> <li>Strict validation is the entry ticket for evidence. A run bundle that cannot pass the applicable strict checks does not support a result claim.</li> <li>Measurement boundaries follow D-018. Claims must name the boundary label where it matters, for example <code>M3 Max / MLX / powermetrics SoC rails</code>, <code>RTX / vLLM / nvidia-smi board power</code>, or <code>wall_meter AC</code>.</li> <li>Cross-boundary comparisons are descriptive only unless a named calibration bundle exists for the compared boundaries. Calibration bundles include wall meter or USB-C PD evidence that explicitly bridges the boundary.</li> <li>Comparative claims from 2M use the experiment manifest order. Interleaved order is required where model reload and operational constraints permit; if block order is forced, the claim must say so and remain below L2 unless the Phase 4 drift audit clears it.</li> <li>Detection-floor gates follow Phase 4 Stage 4.0 and Stage 4.5. Effects below the floor are reported as <code>not resolvable</code>, not as wins, losses, or no difference.</li> <li>Energy-per-output-token claims require runtime-observed output token counts, the runtime stop reason, and the output policy label. If the denominator comes from config fallback rather than runtime observation, the claim downgrades to L0 capability language.</li> <li>(2026-07-09) Token-denominated metrics and cross-tokenizer comparison language follow <code>docs/contracts/token_normalization.md</code>, including its stack-identity table, across all surfaces this ladder governs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ladder">Ladder</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Level</th> <th>Allowed Claim Shape</th> <th>Required Evidence</th> <th>Forbidden Language</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>L0 - Capability</td> <td>The harness can execute this path and preserve auditable evidence.</td> <td>One complete bundle; applicable strict validation; raw artifacts present; boundary label recorded. Config-fallback token denominators may appear only here.</td> <td>faster, cheaper, more efficient, scales, crossover, ranking, law, proves</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L1 - Instrument Result</td> <td>On this exact stack, boundary, workload, and output policy, this measured quantity was observed.</td> <td>n &gt;= 3 strict-valid bundles, or a single run only if explicitly labeled smoke/capability; runtime-observed token counts for per-token claims; stop reason and output policy label; no suspect quality flags unless waived in text.</td> <td>general device ranking, model-family law, cross-target winner, active-parameter scaling result</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L2 - Comparative Result</td> <td>Condition A differed from condition B within the same measurement boundary under a named workload and policy.</td> <td>n &gt;= 5 per condition; strict-valid bundles; 2M experiment manifest order recorded and interleaved where permitted; confidence intervals reported; effect clears the Phase 4 detection floor; same boundary label, or a named calibration bundle if boundaries differ.</td> <td>cross-boundary winner without calibration, universal, architecture-wide conclusion, extrapolated crossover</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L3 - Model Fit</td> <td>A fitted fixed/marginal model predicts held-out cells within stated error for the tested matrix.</td> <td>Designed matrix with holdout cells; strict-valid source bundles; runtime-observed token denominators; residual and sensitivity analysis; detection-floor audit for every fitted effect; boundaries and workload policies stated.</td> <td>law, universal scaling, architecture-wide result, causal language beyond the fitted variables</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L4 - Generalized Finding</td> <td>The finding holds across named stacks, units, or calibrated boundaries under stated limits.</td> <td>Independent replication across a second target or second unit; strict-valid bundles; n and order rules satisfied per condition; named calibration bundles for cross-boundary quantitative comparison; replicated runbook; sensitivity audit survives boundary and version changes.</td> <td>unqualified claims outside tested hardware, workloads, runtime versions, policies, or calibration scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</h2> <ul> <li>Two strict-valid Mac/MLX/powermetrics points that differ in model size, architecture, and quantization are hypothesis-generating for Q4. They are not an active-parameter scaling result.</li> <li>A same-boundary energy/token difference with runtime-observed token counts but fewer than five interleaved repetitions is L1 until the comparative protocol is satisfied.</li> <li>A per-token result using configured output length because runtime token counts were unavailable is L0 capability language, even if the bundle is otherwise strict-valid.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

.codex-bridge/20260807T162304Z-25921-new.log:14144:docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \
.codex-bridge/20260807T162304Z-25921-new.log:14228:docs/process_traces/2026-08-03-d111-backfill/coldgate_d100_bii/refuter-2-nested-closure.md:90:**The distinction that survives, as a condition:** an allowlist enumeration is different in kind from a denylist enumeration **iff** (i) membership is decidable over a finite admitted set, **and** (ii) the admitted set is *derived from producer code and verified to contain every value emitted by the producer across the governed corpus* — D-097's own standard, met explicitly there ("verified: run_campaign.py emits only v1; ... zero v2 manifests across all 29 corpora", decision_log:5946-5948). A hand-derived allowlist satisfies (i) but not (ii), and (ii) is where this project has failed three times. Corollary: C-A's exactness posture is the one D-105 struck; C-C's superset form is nearer the ratified pattern.

id="d-078-soundness-gate-no-claim-bearing-extraction-from-time-anchor-defective-powermetrics-corpora">D-078: Soundness gate — no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. The following spellings are the binding, closed registry for D-078 claim refusals and campaign conditions. Consumers preserve these strings verbatim; an unknown claim/refusal spelling never becomes a pass.</p> <ul> <li>Reducer/analysis claim barriers: <code>nonpositive_window_duration</code>, and <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li>Floor-extraction refusals: <code>bundle_missing</code>, <code>summary_unreadable</code>, <code>bundle_strict_invalid</code>,
