review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
.codex-bridge/20260807T162808Z-37531-new.log:5138:docs/site/project_status_full.html:9:</code></pre> <p>Key elements:</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>Single controller, flexible transports.</strong> <code>local</code> for one-machine runs; <code>ssh</code> for remote NVIDIA/Orin targets and split experiments.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Two adapter layers.</strong> Runtime adapters answer how a model workload executes; telemetry adapters answer how power and thermal state are measured. They are independent, so any runtime can pair with any telemetry source.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>A target is a composition</strong> of transport + runtime + telemetry:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Target</th> <th>Transport</th> <th>Runtime</th> <th>Telemetry</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>macbook_m3_max</td> <td>local</td> <td>mlx</td> <td>powermetrics</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_3050</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>vllm (llama.cpp-CUDA fallback)</td> <td>nvidia-smi</td> </tr> <tr> <td>orin_nano</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>tbd</td> <td>board rails (INA3221)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>pi5_hailo</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>hailo - unsupported (verdict 2026-06-12)</td> <td>wall meter</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> </li> <li><p><strong>Every run writes a self-contained run bundle</strong>: normalized config, device/environment metadata, timestamped event log (lifecycle + phase + token events), raw power trace, backend-native raw telemetry preserved verbatim, logs, model outputs, and reduced summary metrics. Summary numbers are always derived, re-derivable artifacts; the raw bundle is the source of truth.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Typed schemas</strong> (Python dataclasses, standard library only in the core) validate configs and outputs and emit JSON Schema documentation.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Unsupported is a result, not a crash.</strong> Infeasible hardware/model/runtime combinations return structured failure codes (<code>did_not_fit</code>, <code>runtime_unavailable</code>, <code>telemetry_unavailable</code>, ...) and still produce complete bundles - hardware applicability is itself reportable data (this is how a negative Hailo verdict stays a finding).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Dashboard v1 is a read-only run browser</strong>, generated as static HTML from bundles (run table, per-run pages, power traces with phase shading). It has no orchestration role.</p> </li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-methodology-highlights">Measurement Methodology Highlights</h2> <p>Unless a figure explicitly states otherwise, JouleWise uses gross measured energy within the named measurement boundary as the headline basis. Gross energy retains the idle, model-residency, and runtime overhead present during the measured interval, so comparisons across devices, configurations, and split versus monolithic execution use gross energy. Idle-subtracted energy is reported separately as a within-device secondary view of activity above the measured idle baseline; it is not used to rank devices or configurations. In Q4, the fixed term is estimated from the gross-energy workload sweep and is not set equal to measured idle energy.</p> <p>This reporting choice follows Dr. Rivoire&#39;s advisor review, as recorded in D-067: subtracting idle penalizes energy-proportional devices and rewards high-idle ones; for split runs, subtracting both nodes&#39; idles deletes exactly the cost that the Q1 crossover question adjudicates.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Dual-basis capture.</strong> Every eligible measured request records gross and idle-subtracted energy plus idle variance; the reporting rule above changes no stored evidence (D-067).</li> <li><strong>Measurement boundaries are named, not assumed.</strong> Each telemetry backend measures a different physical boundary - powermetrics: Apple SoC subsystems (CPU+GPU+ANE); nvidia-smi: GPU board only; Jetson rails: module input; wall meter: full system AC. Within-target comparisons are the primary claim type; cross-target comparisons always state the boundary difference, calibrated against the wall meter where available.</li> <li><strong>Uncertainty is quantified.</strong> Headline comparisons use n&gt;=5 repetitions with mean, standard deviation, and 95% t-intervals; outliers are flagged (never silently dropped); raw points appear in every figure. Differences are claimed only from the confidence interval of the predeclared paired/block difference or named model contrast — never from marginal-interval separation — with the D-053 three-way wording rule (below-floor: not resolvable; above-floor non-directional: unresolved; equivalence only via a predeclared gate). Thermal state is controlled with an idle-power-recovery gate between repetitions.</li> <li><strong>Multi-node clock discipline.</strong> For split runs, per-node clock offset is bounded with controller-mediated marker events and recorded; cross-node intervals shorter than the bound are flagged rather than trusted.</li> <li><strong>Measurement quality is first-class data</strong>: requested vs observed sampling rate, dropped samples, idle variance, thermal drift, telemetry source - all in every summary.</li> </ul> <h2 id="experiment-plan">Experiment Plan</h2> <p><strong>Homogeneous baselines (Phase 2).</strong> Per target and model: a workload matrix spanning prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, and balanced profiles (prompt 128-4096 tokens x decode 64-512), n=5, producing energy/token and energy/request with intervals - and reproducing the qualitative prefill/decode power asymmetry that motivates disaggregation.</p> <p><strong>Disaggregation (Phase 3), feasibility-first.</strong> KV-cache portability is the project&#39;s central technical risk, so the phase is a ladder where each rung is publishable even if the next fails:</p> <ol> <li><em>Synthetic transfer microbenchmark</em> (guaranteed): move KV-sized payloads between nodes with both-end power sampling - transfer energy and time vs payload size vs link speed, independent of any LLM runtime&#39;s cooperation.</li> <li><em>Offline replay</em> (primary): persist the prompt cache on the prefill node, transfer the file, resume decode on the decode node - same pinned runtime on both ends. Per-runtime feasibility spikes (mlx-lm, llama.cpp including cross-machine portability, vLLM time-boxed) run before any borrowed-hardware scheduling.</li> <li><em>Live split</em> (stretch): streamed KV during the run; explicitly droppable without harming the study.</li> </ol> <p>Payload sizes are analytically predictable (2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes per token, fp16), which drives experiment design - for a 2048-token prompt: a 1.5B-class model ~56 MiB (~0.5 s at 1GbE), an 8B-class model ~256 MiB (~2.3 s at 1GbE). At 1GbE, mid-size-model transfer time is the same order as prefill time on weaker devices - exactly the regime where an energy crossover can exist; the sweep spans prompt lengths and link speeds accordingly.</p> <p><strong>Analysis (Phase 4).</strong> Aggregation over validated bundles with an exclusion log (no silent data drops); a deterministic figure pipeline (every report figure regenerates from a script); a claims-to-evidence index (every quantitative claim traces to figure -&gt; script -&gt; raw bundles); a sensitivity audit checking that headline effects exceed their confidence intervals.</p> <h2 id="phase-plan-detail">Phase Plan Detail</h2> <p>Each phase has a step-by-step plan and an evidence-gated exit checklist in the repository; a phase closes only when every required item has recorded evidence or a documented blocker.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Phase 1</strong> - <code>docs/phase_1/</code>: lock contracts and methodology (done); gather feasibility evidence: advisor scope, Mac telemetry permissions, wall-meter decision, network topology for the sweep, Hailo verdict, NVIDIA/Orin access, calendar mapping.</li> <li><strong>Phase 2</strong> - <code>docs/phase_2/</code>: bundle writer -&gt; mock adapters -&gt; controller -&gt; reducer -&gt; one-command run (all hardware-independent, exact-arithmetic tests) -&gt; then the real Mac slice (MLX + powermetrics, repeated with variance) -&gt; remote targets as access permits -&gt; homogeneous baselines.</li> <li><strong>Phase 3</strong> - <code>docs/phase_3/</code>: feasibility spikes -&gt; split-run config schema -&gt; transfer microbenchmark -&gt; offline-replay splits with per-stage energy decomposition (prefill / transfer / deserialize / decode) -&gt; interconnect sweep -&gt; crossover dataset.</li> <li><strong>Phase 4</strong> - <code>docs/phase_4/</code>: statistics ratification, aggregation, figures F1-F12 (baselines, traces, phase asymmetry, split decomposition, crossover curves, Pareto frontier, interconnect costs, measurement quality), claims index, results + limitations draft, background / related-work draft (new stage 4.6 — the report&#39;s background chapter now has an owner).</li> <li><strong>Phase 5</strong> - <code>docs/phase_5/</code>: verified README quickstart, backend extension guide (verified by a shipped tutorial adapter), sample bundles, dataset freeze with hash manifest and release tag, colloquium slides, final report.</li> </ul> <h2 id="evolution-from-the-original-architecture-sketch">Evolution From The Original Architecture Sketch</h2> <p>The project began from the &quot;Energy Benchmark Architecture And Expanded Plan&quot; sketch. Its architecture survives intact; implementation thinking has been refined in documented ways (full rationale in <code>docs/decision_log.md</code>):</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Original sketch</th> <th>Current position</th> <th>Why</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Configs YAML/JSON; bundle stores <code>config.yaml</code></td> <td>JSON now; bundle stores normalized <code>config.json</code>; YAML deferred until authoring pain is real</td> <td>zero-dependency core; sorted-key JSON gives stable config hashing for aggregation (D-001, D-007)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>&quot;Likely Python + Pydantic&quot; schemas</td> <td>stdlib dataclasses with the same contract; Pydantic port possible later</td> <td>Phase 1 runs with no installs; semantics unchanged (D-009)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Mac MLX slice implemented first</td> <td>mock vertical slice first, Mac immediately after</td> <td>the harness is proven with exact-arithmetic tests before real telemetry can confound it; Mac remains the first real backend (Phase 2 plan)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Dashboard file-backed; &quot;DuckDB/SQLite if browsing gets slow&quot;</td> <td>static HTML generator; analysis aggregation via CSV + pandas in Phase 4; no DB planned</td> <td>smallest sustainable tool that serves the two real uses: sanity-checking runs and showing progress (D-006)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Offline KV replay before live disaggregation</td> <td>same, hardened into a three-rung feasibility ladder with per-runtime spikes and a same-runtime rule</td> <td>KV tensors are not portable across engines; cross-runtime transfer (e.g. vLLM-prefill -&gt; MLX-decode) is out of scope; heterogeneous <em>hardware</em> pairs use a portable runtime where its backends allow, pending an explicit portability spike (D-015)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPU-to-Apple split experiments listed directly</td> <td>pairings are planned only after spike verdicts; synthetic transfer sweep guarantees the crossover dataset either way</td> <td>converts the project&#39;s largest feasibility risk into a bounded one (R-004, R-005)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>(not covered)</td> <td>measurement boundaries, multi-node clock discipline, controller co-residency mitigation, statistical protocol</td> <td>added rigor required for defensible cross-device energy claims (D-003, D-013, D-014, D-018)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Verdict from the 2026-06-09 audit: the sketch remains coherent; nothing in it has been contradicted - the changes above are refinements with recorded rationale, and the repository&#39;s plans are the maintained, authoritative version of it.</p> <h2 id="risks-and-minimum-viable-outcome">Risks And Minimum Viable Outcome</h2> <p>Top risks (full register with triggers and fallbacks in <code>docs/risk_register.md</code>):</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Risk</th> <th>Posture</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>KV persist/resume unsupported in a runtime (esp. vLLM)</td> <td>spikes before hardware scheduling; llama.cpp fallback; synthetic-transfer floor + analytical composition keeps the study publishable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Cache files not portable across machines/backends</td> <td>explicit cross-machine spike; fallback to same-platform pairs; portability finding is itself reportable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Schedule vs fixed academic deadlines</td> <td>every phase has a hardware-independent floor; explicit descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3080 Ti borrow window slips</td> <td>borrow time is execution-only against a rehearsed runbook; pairing droppable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>No wall meter</td> <td>within-target claims unaffected; cross-target claims carry the stated boundary caveat</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Advisor approval delay</td> <td>all current work is harness-shaped and valuable under any scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Minimum viable outcome (worst-case floor; still a complete, defensible capstone if reached): the reusable harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + an analytical split-energy model - honest, measured, reproducible.</p> <h2 id="timeline">Timeline</h2> <p>Dates pending (this is an explicit ask): colloquium date, report deadline, borrow window. Once known they anchor <code>docs/milestones.md</code> and phase target dates are derived backwards (slides want frozen figures &gt;=1 week ahead; the report wants its claims audit &gt;=1 week ahead). Until then, the dependency structure is the schedule: Phase 4 is deskwork and serves as the buffer; hardware-gated steps are scheduled around access windows with desk work filling gaps.</p> <p>Known: the Mac authorization gate closed 2026-07-06 (privileged sample captured, scoped sudo rule installed); remote-device access (NVIDIA, Orin) is the remaining hardware gate. Work paused 2026-06-13 to 2026-07-04 (planned break, recorded in <code>docs/milestones.md</code>).</p> <h2 id="deliverables-at-completion">Deliverables At Completion</h2> <ul> <li>The JouleWise repository: harness, adapters, tests, CI, extension guide, README quickstart that a new user can run in minutes.</li> <li>The dataset: raw run bundles + hash manifest, frozen and tagged, with every figure regenerable by script.</li> <li>The study: where splitting wins, loses, and why - with uncertainty, limitations, and hardware-applicability findings (including negative verdicts).</li> <li>Final report and colloquium presentation, every quantitative claim traceable to raw data.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repository-map-for-verification">Repository Map (for verification)</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Where</th> <th>What</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>README.md</code></td> <td>entry point and quickstart (grows in Phase 5)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code></td> <td>phase index and acceptance criteria</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/phase_N/phase_N_plan.md</code> + <code>_exit_checklist.md</code></td> <td>per-phase steps and evidence gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/</code></td> <td>measurement methodology, run-bundle layout, adapter contracts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></td> <td>every design decision with alternatives considered</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/risk_register.md</code></td> <td>risks, triggers, mitigations, descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/milestones.md</code></td> <td>calendar map</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/run_reports/</code></td> <td>dated work logs with commands and outcomes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code></td> <td>the harness package + canonical test suite; the command and CI output own its current result</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="process-note">Process Note</h2> <p>The machinery exists to protect measurement claims from unchecked summaries, stale assumptions, and review-induced drift.</p> <p>This project is developed by a human researcher directing a multi-agent AI system he designed and iteratively engineered over the course of the project — the orchestration itself is a second, deliberate piece of engineering alongside the measurement harness and its benchmark, and by now it is interesting in its own right.</p> <p>The full description lives in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> (the loop, the roles, the artifact system, and how the topology itself evolved under its own review machinery); this section is the summary.</p> <p><strong>The division of labor.</strong> Ed sets the research direction, the methodology standards (the decision log&#39;s non-negotiables: raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy headlines, named measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), the hardware and access decisions, and — the part that is easy to underrate — the <em>process policy</em>: every rule below exists because he observed a failure or an opportunity and issued a standing instruction. The AI staff executes: the designated lead agent is the final reviewer and single point of accountability: decomposition, design adjudication, every final diff gate, live verification, merges, and bookkeeping. Independent implementation and review agents do the volume work against pinned specs, adversarial review lenses, test writing, and fresh-instance test auditing; specialist agents handle bounded sweeps. Cross-model review is load-bearing by design: the attributed catch record shows the models and review layers catching different classes of defect.</p> <p><strong>The machinery, briefly.</strong> Independent tasks run as parallel git worktrees, the lead driving each stream&#39;s implementation/review pipeline directly (a topology that is itself the product of a signed cross-model meta-review, then validated by a full session with zero coordination stalls — the evolution is traced in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code>). Every implementation passes through a layered pipeline: a design argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before coding), fresh-instance counterreview lenses with lead-triaged dispositions, a test-amplification round, a writer-never-reviews-its-own-tests audit, the lead&#39;s diff gate, and lead-side live verification on real hardware — the one layer never delegated, because it has repeatedly caught blockers whose own tests were green (the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code). Merges add their own gate: a pre-merge oversight pass by fresh reviewers with distinct angles, and a standing <em>final-head rule</em> — any commit landing after the last review round gets one more fresh review before merge (its first application caught a crash path in a &quot;trivial&quot; late fix). After parallel streams merge, a dedicated integration review hunts the cross-stream defects no per-stream review can see (two interaction defects on its first outing, two more on its second). An event-driven review council convenes for contract-bearing work, and — per Ed&#39;s instruction — its <em>deliberations</em> are recorded, not just its verdicts: the council log preserves positions, the reasoning exchanged, who prevailed and why, and overridden dissents, so a future reader (or model) can reconstruct why any decision was made.</p> <p><strong>The paper trail (each claim traceable to its evidence home; the external re-reduction demonstration is still pending).</strong> Each fact has one home: <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> — the binding design decisions (the log is the count authority), most recording alternatives considered and revisit conditions; <code>docs/council_log.md</code> — the deliberation record; <code>docs/stream_logs/</code> — per-stream decision ledgers committed <em>with</em> the code they justify (wrong decisions are superseded in place, never erased); <code>docs/run_reports/</code> — one record per session with verification evidence, a per-review-layer catch table, and a delegation-calibration ledger (outcomes assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-reported; prompt-defects separated from model-defects). The whole loop is self-instrumenting: every review layer&#39;s unique catches are attributed and tallied, and a layer that stops earning its keep is dropped by its own evidence rule (one already has been). Delegation boundaries move on calibration evidence, not intuition. Lessons are folded into the process playbooks the same session they are learned — measurably: one failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, and zero times after. The loop even reviews itself: a meta-review consensus (C-009) redesigned the coordination topology, and the next session (C-010) validated the redesign with a zero-stall run.</p> <p><strong>What one day of this looks like (2026-07-07).</strong> Five implementation streams plus a repo-wide test audit ran concurrently: statistical uncertainty, contamination detection, deep DVFS telemetry, campaign automation, and a KV-cache size model. All five merged the same day; the test suite grew 254 → 369; the layered review recorded thirteen attributed catches including three blockers that no single reviewer would plausibly have found together. One blocker surfaced only when the real CLI was run against code whose own tests were green, because the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.</p> <p><strong>How the scope grew.</strong> The project began as an architecture sketch for &quot;measure LLM inference energy on edge hardware.&quot; Contracts-first engineering turned that into an auditable instrument: typed configs, self-contained evidence bundles, a strict re-reduction validator. The mock vertical slice proved the math without hardware; the Mac slice produced the first real joules; the flagship run put a 122-billion- parameter mixture-of-experts model through the identical harness and yielded the first real cross-model observation: two confounded points that differ in size, architecture, and quantization, with energy/token behavior consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal model while decode power stays nearly flat — the big model costs time, not watts. This week the instrument gained the statistical and forensic machinery above, and a steelmanned, devil&#39;s-advocated research agenda of 31 tiered questions — 16 answerable on the current hardware alone (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The pattern throughout: capability first, claims only when the instrument can defend them.</p> <p><strong>And the most recent day (2026-07-07/08).</strong> Four checkpointed streams were resumed, completed, and merged in one session: the integrity/ provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed; strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence), the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded ~30 attributed catches, including two blockers no implementer&#39;s tests could see (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation input; a validation-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire contracts overturned by review before they could ever touch hardware, and one fabricated-evidence defect caught only at the lead&#39;s diff gate. The suite went 415 → 546 tests with zero expected failures, and the lead never wrote implementation code and never skipped a gate.</p> <p><strong>Where to look.</strong> <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> is the process description. <code>docs/council_log.md</code> is the deliberation record — C-006 is a full orchestration trace of the five-stream day; C-009/C-010 are the topology meta-review and its validation; C-011 is the critique counter-review. <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> holds the binding design decisions with alternatives considered (the log is the count authority). <code>docs/run_reports/</code> narrates each working session, with per-layer catch tables and the delegation-calibration ledger. The executable orchestration playbooks live outside this repository as reusable skills (council, delegation, multi-stream worktrees, adversarial review, and a top-level operation-loop that sequences them), so the machinery survives this project and transfers to the next one.</p> <h2 id="maintenance-of-this-document">Maintenance Of This Document</h2> <p>Updated at phase transitions and whenever advisor-visible state changes (a gate closes, a verdict lands, the schedule moves). Volatile work-selection facts stay in the state kernel, verification results stay in command/CI output, and decision structure stays in the checked decision-log index. A front-facing change also refreshes <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code>; Ed alone regenerates and deploys the site (D-068).</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>PROJECT_STATUS.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
.codex-bridge/20260807T162808Z-37531-new.log:5143:docs/site/research.html:17:</header> <main> <section class="learn-hero"> <div class="kicker">Interactive field guide · programming knowledge assumed · measurement science taught here</div> <p class="readme-eyebrow">From watts to warranted claims.</p> <h1>How do you measure<br>a machine thinking?</h1> <p class="lede">You already know how programs execute. This guide adds the uncomfortable part: deciding which physical signal belongs to the program, how much noise the instrument adds, and what the evidence actually permits you to say.</p> <nav class="chapter-nav" aria-label="Guide chapters"> <a href="#hard">The hard part</a><a href="#units">Watts &amp; joules</a> <a href="#sampling">Sampling</a><a href="#bundles">Bundles</a> <a href="#floor">Detection floors</a><a href="#found">Findings</a> <a href="#next">Next</a> </nav> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span> <span class="source-chip" title="docs/site_src/research.html · commit 05002b1"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>site_src/<wbr>research.html</span><span class="source-commit">commit 05002b1</span></span></div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="hard"> <div class="chapter-number">01</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Why this is hard</div> <h2>The model does not come with an energy return value.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A profiler can tell you which function consumed CPU time. Energy is a physical quantity observed through a separate instrument. You have to align two clocks, define a boundary, and decide what else was happening while the model ran.</p> <div class="concept-grid"> <article><span>Boundary</span><h3>Which power?</h3><p>SoC rails omit parts of the whole machine. Wall power includes more than the chip. Neither is automatically wrong; an unlabeled boundary is.</p></article> <article><span>Attribution</span><h3>Which interval?</h3><p>Load the model too late or stop sampling too early and the number answers a different question than the experiment config asked.</p></article> <article><span>Workload</span><h3>Which work?</h3><p>Prompt length, generated tokens, batching, caching, stop behavior, and content can all change the physical execution.</p></article> <article><span>Noise</span><h3>Which difference?</h3><p>Background activity, thermal state, sampling cadence, clock error, and run order can manufacture a small “effect.”</p></article> </div> <aside class="learn-aside"><strong>The measurement-science move:</strong> replace “I got a number” with “I defined a quantity, captured the evidence, bounded what could imitate it, and stated the claim ceiling.”</aside> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="units"> <div class="chapter-number">02</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Watts, joules, and idle</div> <h2>Power is a rate. Energy is the area.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A watt is one joule per second. If power changes over time, energy is the integral under the power trace. That identity is a unit definition—not a JouleWise measurement result.</p> <div class="equation-stack"> <div><span>instantaneous power</span><strong>P(t)</strong><small>watts = joules / second</small></div> <div><span>gross measured energy</span><strong>E = ∫ P(t) dt</strong><small>headline basis within the named boundary</small></div> <div><span>idle-subtracted energy</span><strong>E<sub>secondary</sub> = ∫ (P(t) − P<sub>idle</sub>) dt</strong><small>within-device secondary view only</small></div> </div> <p>Idle is not “free energy to erase.” It is an observed baseline under a stated condition. Subtracting it can help describe activity above baseline on one device, but it can distort comparisons: a high-idle device gets a larger subtraction. JouleWise therefore uses <strong>gross energy for every cross-device, cross-configuration, and split-vs-monolithic headline</strong>. Phase energy is gross-only.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="sampling"> <div class="chapter-number">03</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">How powermetrics sampling works</div> <h2>You never see the continuous curve.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede"><code>powermetrics</code> reports discrete samples from named Apple power rails. JouleWise aligns those samples with runtime events and integrates between explicit measured-window boundaries. Move the toy controls below: the underlying program is unchanged, but the estimated area changes when the window or sample pattern changes.</p> <div class="interactive-card" data-trace-lab> <div The interesting part is what strict validation does with it.</p> <div class="bundle-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Run bundle artifacts flow through strict validation to a bounded claim"> <div class="bundle-box"><span>run bundle</span><code>config.json</code><code>metadata.json</code><code>events.jsonl</code><code>raw telemetry</code><code>outputs + logs</code><code>summary metrics</code></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">replay →</div> <div class="bundle-box validator-box"><span>strict validator</span><p>parse raw evidence</p><p>re-derive windows</p><p>recompute energy</p><p>check provenance</p><p>fail on mismatch</p></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">gate →</div> <div class="bundle-box claim-box"><span>claim ceiling</span><p>L0: auditability</p><p>L1: descriptive</p><p>L2+: only after floor, uncertainty, plan, and evidence gates</p></div> </div> <p><strong>Strict-valid does not mean scientifically conclusive.</strong> It means the recorded artifact is internally valid under the strict contract. A bundle can be strict-valid and still carry flags that prevent a comparison claim. That distinction matters in the newest floor data.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="floor"> <div class="chapter-number">05</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Detection floors</div> <h2>How small is too small to resolve?</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">Repeat the same condition and the measured energy moves anyway. The false-effect guard floor summarizes how large that repeat scatter—or an ABBA comparison artifact—can look. An effect below the applicable floor is <strong>not resolvable</strong>, not proven absent.</p> <div class="interactive-card floor-lab" data-floor-lab> <div class="interactive-head"><div><span class="card-label">Effect-versus-floor gate</span><h3>Try to clear a real verified floor.</h3></div><span class="status-chip">calibration logic</span></div> <label class="floor-select">Choose the applicable gate <select data-floor-select> <option value="0.527197" data-basis="gross request · absolute repeat">Gross mid-request absolute · 0.527197 J</option> <option value="0.909237" data-basis="gross request · comparative ABBA">Gross mid-request comparative · 0.909237 J</option> <option value="0.536632" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary">Idle-subtracted mid-request absolute · 0.536632 J</option> <option value="0.894215" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary comparative">Idle-subtracted mid-request comparative · 0.894215 J</option> <option value="1.738940" data-basis="gross prefill phase · governing gate">Gross prefill phase gate · 1.738940 J</option> <option value="1.026892" data-basis="gross decode phase · governing gate">Gross decode phase gate · 1.026892 J</option> <option value="4.922865" data-basis="gross suite-item · governing gate">Gross suite-item gate · 4.922865 J</option> <option value="24.618735" data-basis="gross suite-level · governing gate">Gross suite-level gate · 24.618735 J</option> </select> </label> <label class="effect-control">Hypothetical observed effect <input data-effect type="range" min="0" max="30" value="0.70" step="0.01"> <output data-effect-out>0.70 J</output> </label> <div class="floor-track" aria-hidden="true"><span data-floor-mark></span><i data-effect-mark></i></div> <div class="floor-verdict" data-floor-verdict aria-live="polite"></div> <p class="interactive-note">Clearing this numeric gate is necessary, not sufficient. It does not clear clock, sampling, uncertainty, contamination, multiplicity, correctness, or pre-registered analysis-plan gates.</p> </div> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md · commit 907ee58"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>phase_2/<wbr>detection_floor.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 907ee58</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="found"> <div class="chapter-number">06</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">What the project has found so far</div> <h2>Real floors, plus an important warning.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">The verified Window-A extraction reports the following false-effect guard floors. Comparative values use ABBA blocks; “gate” is the larger applicable absolute/comparative value.
