.codex-bridge/20260807T162808Z-37531-new.log:5144:docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \
.codex-bridge/20260807T162808Z-37531-new.log:5148:docs/site/claims_ladder.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>Claims Ladder - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#global-rules">Global Rules</a> <a href="#ladder">Ladder</a> <a href="#downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-contracts-claims-ladder-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Claims Ladder</h1> <p>Status: binding for reader-facing claims from Slice 2M onward. Decision D-037 records adoption. Per-claim IDs and mechanical enforcement arrive with the Phase 4 claims index; until then, authors apply this ladder during review.</p> <p>This contract governs wording in reports, slides, README/status prose, figure captions, and tables that a reader could treat as a result. Dated run reports, stream logs, council logs, and decision logs may preserve historical wording, but later reader-facing summaries must use the current level.</p> <p>The warning-only prose scan mechanically enumerates <code>README.md</code>, <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>docs/report_src/**</code>, the generated Phase-4 claims projection, Markdown tables/captions under analysis and figure artifacts, and present or future <code>slides/</code>, <code>captions/</code>, and <code>tables/</code> publication trees. Historical <code>docs/run_reports/**</code> records and the decision/council/stream logs are deliberately outside that scan. Warning-only exit behavior remains the D-059 policy: these findings require editorial review but are not structural claim-gate failures.</p> <p>The canonical JSONL accepts two authority-distinct row dialects through one fail-closed validator: the single pre-P2-037 legacy L1 row only under its exact hash-pinned identity, and current rows linked to a governed <code>joulewise.claim_verdicts.v1</code> artifact. Rows with unknown authority fields or a mixture of legacy and engine-linked authority fields are invalid. Verdict semantics belong to <code>joulewise.analysis_engine</code>; the claims-index layer adds only linkage, canonical ordering/rendering, relative-path, editorial, and current production-admission checks. <code>two_look_alpha_spending</code> remains outside claims-index production admission until separately ruled in; current admission is deliberately <code>fixed_n</code> only.</p> <h2 id="global-rules">Global Rules</h2> <ul> <li>Strict validation is the entry ticket for evidence. A run bundle that cannot pass the applicable strict checks does not support a result claim.</li> <li>Measurement boundaries follow D-018. Claims must name the boundary label where it matters, for example <code>M3 Max / MLX / powermetrics SoC rails</code>, <code>RTX / vLLM / nvidia-smi board power</code>, or <code>wall_meter AC</code>.</li> <li>Cross-boundary comparisons are descriptive only unless a named calibration bundle exists for the compared boundaries. Calibration bundles include wall meter or USB-C PD evidence that explicitly bridges the boundary.</li> <li>Comparative claims from 2M use the experiment manifest order. Interleaved order is required where model reload and operational constraints permit; if block order is forced, the claim must say so and remain below L2 unless the Phase 4 drift audit clears it.</li> <li>Detection-floor gates follow Phase 4 Stage 4.0 and Stage 4.5. Effects below the floor are reported as <code>not resolvable</code>, not as wins, losses, or no difference.</li> <li>Energy-per-output-token claims require runtime-observed output token counts, the runtime stop reason, and the output policy label. If the denominator comes from config fallback rather than runtime observation, the claim downgrades to L0 capability language.</li> <li>(2026-07-09) Token-denominated metrics and cross-tokenizer comparison language follow <code>docs/contracts/token_normalization.md</code>, including its stack-identity table, across all surfaces this ladder governs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ladder">Ladder</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Level</th> <th>Allowed Claim Shape</th> <th>Required Evidence</th> <th>Forbidden Language</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>L0 - Capability</td> <td>The harness can execute this path and preserve auditable evidence.</td> <td>One complete bundle; applicable strict validation; raw artifacts present; boundary label recorded. Config-fallback token denominators may appear only here.</td> <td>faster, cheaper, more efficient, scales, crossover, ranking, law, proves</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L1 - Instrument Result</td> <td>On this exact stack, boundary, workload, and output policy, this measured quantity was observed.</td> <td>n &gt;= 3 strict-valid bundles, or a single run only if explicitly labeled smoke/capability; runtime-observed token counts for per-token claims; stop reason and output policy label; no suspect quality flags unless waived in text.</td> <td>general device ranking, model-family law, cross-target winner, active-parameter scaling result</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L2 - Comparative Result</td> <td>Condition A differed from condition B within the same measurement boundary under a named workload and policy.</td> <td>n &gt;= 5 per condition; strict-valid bundles; 2M experiment manifest order recorded and interleaved where permitted; confidence intervals reported; effect clears the Phase 4 detection floor; same boundary label, or a named calibration bundle if boundaries differ.</td> <td>cross-boundary winner without calibration, universal, architecture-wide conclusion, extrapolated crossover</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L3 - Model Fit</td> <td>A fitted fixed/marginal model predicts held-out cells within stated error for the tested matrix.</td> <td>Designed matrix with holdout cells; strict-valid source bundles; runtime-observed token denominators; residual and sensitivity analysis; detection-floor audit for every fitted effect; boundaries and workload policies stated.</td> <td>law, universal scaling, architecture-wide result, causal language beyond the fitted variables</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L4 - Generalized Finding</td> <td>The finding holds across named stacks, units, or calibrated boundaries under stated limits.</td> <td>Independent replication across a second target or second unit; strict-valid bundles; n and order rules satisfied per condition; named calibration bundles for cross-boundary quantitative comparison; replicated runbook; sensitivity audit survives boundary and version changes.</td> <td>unqualified claims outside tested hardware, workloads, runtime versions, policies, or calibration scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</h2> <ul> <li>Two strict-valid Mac/MLX/powermetrics points that differ in model size, architecture, and quantization are hypothesis-generating for Q4. They are not an active-parameter scaling result.</li> <li>A same-boundary energy/token difference with runtime-observed token counts but fewer than five interleaved repetitions is L1 until the comparative protocol is satisfied.</li> <li>A per-token result using configured output length because runtime token counts were unavailable is L0 capability language, even if the bundle is otherwise strict-valid.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
.codex-bridge/20260807T162808Z-37531-new.log:5211:docs/site/project_status_full.html:9:</code></pre> <p>Key elements:</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>Single controller, flexible transports.</strong> <code>local</code> for one-machine runs; <code>ssh</code> for remote NVIDIA/Orin targets and split experiments.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Two adapter layers.</strong> Runtime adapters answer how a model workload executes; telemetry adapters answer how power and thermal state are measured. They are independent, so any runtime can pair with any telemetry source.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>A target is a composition</strong> of transport + runtime + telemetry:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Target</th> <th>Transport</th> <th>Runtime</th> <th>Telemetry</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>macbook_m3_max</td> <td>local</td> <td>mlx</td> <td>powermetrics</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_3050</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>vllm (llama.cpp-CUDA fallback)</td> <td>nvidia-smi</td> </tr> <tr> <td>orin_nano</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>tbd</td> <td>board rails (INA3221)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>pi5_hailo</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>hailo - unsupported (verdict 2026-06-12)</td> <td>wall meter</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> </li> <li><p><strong>Every run writes a self-contained run bundle</strong>: normalized config, device/environment metadata, timestamped event log (lifecycle + phase + token events), raw power trace, backend-native raw telemetry preserved verbatim, logs, model outputs, and reduced summary metrics. Summary numbers are always derived, re-derivable artifacts; the raw bundle is the source of truth.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Typed schemas</strong> (Python dataclasses, standard library only in the core) validate configs and outputs and emit JSON Schema documentation.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Unsupported is a result, not a crash.</strong> Infeasible hardware/model/runtime combinations return structured failure codes (<code>did_not_fit</code>, <code>runtime_unavailable</code>, <code>telemetry_unavailable</code>, ...) and still produce complete bundles - hardware applicability is itself reportable data (this is how a negative Hailo verdict stays a finding).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Dashboard v1 is a read-only run browser</strong>, generated as static HTML from bundles (run table, per-run pages, power traces with phase shading). It has no orchestration role.</p> </li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-methodology-highlights">Measurement Methodology Highlights</h2> <p>Unless a figure explicitly states otherwise, JouleWise uses gross measured energy within the named measurement boundary as the headline basis. Gross energy retains the idle, model-residency, and runtime overhead present during the measured interval, so comparisons across devices, configurations, and split versus monolithic execution use gross energy. Idle-subtracted energy is reported separately as a within-device secondary view of activity above the measured idle baseline; it is not used to rank devices or configurations. In Q4, the fixed term is estimated from the gross-energy workload sweep and is not set equal to measured idle energy.</p> <p>This reporting choice follows Dr. Rivoire&#39;s advisor review, as recorded in D-067: subtracting idle penalizes energy-proportional devices and rewards high-idle ones; for split runs, subtracting both nodes&#39; idles deletes exactly the cost that the Q1 crossover question adjudicates.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Dual-basis capture.</strong> Every eligible measured request records gross and idle-subtracted energy plus idle variance; the reporting rule above changes no stored evidence (D-067).</li> <li><strong>Measurement boundaries are named, not assumed.</strong> Each telemetry backend measures a different physical boundary - powermetrics: Apple SoC subsystems (CPU+GPU+ANE); nvidia-smi: GPU board only; Jetson rails: module input; wall meter: full system AC. Within-target comparisons are the primary claim type; cross-target comparisons always state the boundary difference, calibrated against the wall meter where available.</li> <li><strong>Uncertainty is quantified.</strong> Headline comparisons use n&gt;=5 repetitions with mean, standard deviation, and 95% t-intervals; outliers are flagged (never silently dropped); raw points appear in every figure. Differences are claimed only from the confidence interval of the predeclared paired/block difference or named model contrast — never from marginal-interval separation — with the D-053 three-way wording rule (below-floor: not resolvable; above-floor non-directional: unresolved; equivalence only via a predeclared gate). Thermal state is controlled with an idle-power-recovery gate between repetitions.</li> <li><strong>Multi-node clock discipline.</strong> For split runs, per-node clock offset is bounded with controller-mediated marker events and recorded; cross-node intervals shorter than the bound are flagged rather than trusted.</li> <li><strong>Measurement quality is first-class data</strong>: requested vs observed sampling rate, dropped samples, idle variance, thermal drift, telemetry source - all in every summary.</li> </ul> <h2 id="experiment-plan">Experiment Plan</h2> <p><strong>Homogeneous baselines (Phase 2).</strong> Per target and model: a workload matrix spanning prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, and balanced profiles (prompt 128-4096 tokens x decode 64-512), n=5, producing energy/token and energy/request with intervals - and reproducing the qualitative prefill/decode power asymmetry that motivates disaggregation.</p> <p><strong>Disaggregation (Phase 3), feasibility-first.</strong> KV-cache portability is the project&#39;s central technical risk, so the phase is a ladder where each rung is publishable even if the next fails:</p> <ol> <li><em>Synthetic transfer microbenchmark</em> (guaranteed): move KV-sized payloads between nodes with both-end power sampling - transfer energy and time vs payload size vs link speed, independent of any LLM runtime&#39;s cooperation.</li> <li><em>Offline replay</em> (primary): persist the prompt cache on the prefill node, transfer the file, resume decode on the decode node - same pinned runtime on both ends. Per-runtime feasibility spikes (mlx-lm, llama.cpp including cross-machine portability, vLLM time-boxed) run before any borrowed-hardware scheduling.</li> <li><em>Live split</em> (stretch): streamed KV during the run; explicitly droppable without harming the study.</li> </ol> <p>Payload sizes are analytically predictable (2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes per token, fp16), which drives experiment design - for a 2048-token prompt: a 1.5B-class model ~56 MiB (~0.5 s at 1GbE), an 8B-class model ~256 MiB (~2.3 s at 1GbE). At 1GbE, mid-size-model transfer time is the same order as prefill time on weaker devices - exactly the regime where an energy crossover can exist; the sweep spans prompt lengths and link speeds accordingly.</p> <p><strong>Analysis (Phase 4).</strong> Aggregation over validated bundles with an exclusion log (no silent data drops); a deterministic figure pipeline (every report figure regenerates from a script); a claims-to-evidence index (every quantitative claim traces to figure -&gt; script -&gt; raw bundles); a sensitivity audit checking that headline effects exceed their confidence intervals.</p> <h2 id="phase-plan-detail">Phase Plan Detail</h2> <p>Each phase has a step-by-step plan and an evidence-gated exit checklist in the repository; a phase closes only when every required item has recorded evidence or a documented blocker.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Phase 1</strong> - <code>docs/phase_1/</code>: lock contracts and methodology (done); gather feasibility evidence: advisor scope, Mac telemetry permissions, wall-meter decision, network topology for the sweep, Hailo verdict, NVIDIA/Orin access, calendar mapping.</li> <li><strong>Phase 2</strong> - <code>docs/phase_2/</code>: bundle writer -&gt; mock adapters -&gt; controller -&gt; reducer -&gt; one-command run (all hardware-independent, exact-arithmetic tests) -&gt; then the real Mac slice (MLX + powermetrics, repeated with variance) -&gt; remote targets as access permits -&gt; homogeneous baselines.</li> <li><strong>Phase 3</strong> - <code>docs/phase_3/</code>: feasibility spikes -&gt; split-run config schema -&gt; transfer microbenchmark -&gt; offline-replay splits with per-stage energy decomposition (prefill / transfer / deserialize / decode) -&gt; interconnect sweep -&gt; crossover dataset.</li> <li><strong>Phase 4</strong> - <code>docs/phase_4/</code>: statistics ratification, aggregation, figures F1-F12 (baselines, traces, phase asymmetry, split decomposition, crossover curves, Pareto frontier, interconnect costs, measurement quality), claims index, results + limitations draft, background / related-work draft (new stage 4.6 — the report&#39;s background chapter now has an owner).</li> <li><strong>Phase 5</strong> - <code>docs/phase_5/</code>: verified README quickstart, backend extension guide (verified by a shipped tutorial adapter), sample bundles, dataset freeze with hash manifest and release tag, colloquium slides, final report.</li> </ul> <h2 id="evolution-from-the-original-architecture-sketch">Evolution From The Original Architecture Sketch</h2> <p>The project began from the &quot;Energy Benchmark Architecture And Expanded Plan&quot; sketch. Its architecture survives intact; implementation thinking has been refined in documented ways (full rationale in <code>docs/decision_log.md</code>):</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Original sketch</th> <th>Current position</th> <th>Why</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Configs YAML/JSON; bundle stores <code>config.yaml</code></td> <td>JSON now; bundle stores normalized <code>config.json</code>; YAML deferred until authoring pain is real</td> <td>zero-dependency core; sorted-key JSON gives stable config hashing for aggregation (D-001, D-007)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>&quot;Likely Python + Pydantic&quot; schemas</td> <td>stdlib dataclasses with the same contract; Pydantic port possible later</td> <td>Phase 1 runs with no installs; semantics unchanged (D-009)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Mac MLX slice implemented first</td> <td>mock vertical slice first, Mac immediately after</td> <td>the harness is proven with exact-arithmetic tests before real telemetry can confound it; Mac remains the first real backend (Phase 2 plan)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Dashboard file-backed; &quot;DuckDB/SQLite if browsing gets slow&quot;</td> <td>static HTML generator; analysis aggregation via CSV + pandas in Phase 4; no DB planned</td> <td>smallest sustainable tool that serves the two real uses: sanity-checking runs and showing progress (D-006)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Offline KV replay before live disaggregation</td> <td>same, hardened into a three-rung feasibility ladder with per-runtime spikes and a same-runtime rule</td> <td>KV tensors are not portable across engines; cross-runtime transfer (e.g. vLLM-prefill -&gt; MLX-decode) is out of scope; heterogeneous <em>hardware</em> pairs use a portable runtime where its backends allow, pending an explicit portability spike (D-015)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPU-to-Apple split experiments listed directly</td> <td>pairings are planned only after spike verdicts; synthetic transfer sweep guarantees the crossover dataset either way</td> <td>converts the project&#39;s largest feasibility risk into a bounded one (R-004, R-005)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>(not covered)</td> <td>measurement boundaries, multi-node clock discipline, controller co-residency mitigation, statistical protocol</td> <td>added rigor required for defensible cross-device energy claims (D-003, D-013, D-014, D-018)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Verdict from the 2026-06-09 audit: the sketch remains coherent; nothing in it has been contradicted - the changes above are refinements with recorded rationale, and the repository&#39;s plans are the maintained, authoritative version of it.</p> <h2 id="risks-and-minimum-viable-outcome">Risks And Minimum Viable Outcome</h2> <p>Top risks (full register with triggers and fallbacks in <code>docs/risk_register.md</code>):</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Risk</th> <th>Posture</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>KV persist/resume unsupported in a runtime (esp. vLLM)</td> <td>spikes before hardware scheduling; llama.cpp fallback; synthetic-transfer floor + analytical composition keeps the study publishable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Cache files not portable across machines/backends</td> <td>explicit cross-machine spike; fallback to same-platform pairs; portability finding is itself reportable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Schedule vs fixed academic deadlines</td> <td>every phase has a hardware-independent floor; explicit descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3080 Ti borrow window slips</td> <td>borrow time is execution-only against a rehearsed runbook; pairing droppable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>No wall meter</td> <td>within-target claims unaffected; cross-target claims carry the stated boundary caveat</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Advisor approval delay</td> <td>all current work is harness-shaped and valuable under any scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Minimum viable outcome (worst-case floor; still a complete, defensible capstone if reached): the reusable harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + an analytical split-energy model - honest, measured, reproducible.</p> <h2 id="timeline">Timeline</h2> <p>Dates pending (this is an explicit ask): colloquium date, report deadline, borrow window. Once known they anchor <code>docs/milestones.md</code> and phase target dates are derived backwards (slides want frozen figures &gt;=1 week ahead; the report wants its claims audit &gt;=1 week ahead). Until then, the dependency structure is the schedule: Phase 4 is deskwork and serves as the buffer; hardware-gated steps are scheduled around access windows with desk work filling gaps.</p> <p>Known: the Mac authorization gate closed 2026-07-06 (privileged sample captured, scoped sudo rule installed); remote-device access (NVIDIA, Orin) is the remaining hardware gate. Work paused 2026-06-13 to 2026-07-04 (planned break, recorded in <code>docs/milestones.md</code>).</p> <h2 id="deliverables-at-completion">Deliverables At Completion</h2> <ul> <li>The JouleWise repository: harness, adapters, tests, CI, extension guide, README quickstart that a new user can run in minutes.</li> <li>The dataset: raw run bundles + hash manifest, frozen and tagged, with every figure regenerable by script.</li> <li>The study: where splitting wins, loses, and why - with uncertainty, limitations, and hardware-applicability findings (including negative verdicts).</li> <li>Final report and colloquium presentation, every quantitative claim traceable to raw data.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repository-map-for-verification">Repository Map (for verification)</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Where</th> <th>What</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>README.md</code></td> <td>entry point and quickstart (grows in Phase 5)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code></td> <td>phase index and acceptance criteria</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/phase_N/phase_N_plan.md</code> + <code>_exit_checklist.md</code></td> <td>per-phase steps and evidence gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/</code></td> <td>measurement methodology, run-bundle layout, adapter contracts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></td> <td>every design decision with alternatives considered</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/risk_register.md</code></td> <td>risks, triggers, mitigations, descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/milestones.md</code></td> <td>calendar map</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/run_reports/</code></td> <td>dated work logs with commands and outcomes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code></td> <td>the harness package + canonical test suite; the command and CI output own its current result</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="process-note">Process Note</h2> <p>The machinery exists to protect measurement claims from unchecked summaries, stale assumptions, and review-induced drift.</p> <p>This project is developed by a human researcher directing a multi-agent AI system he designed and iteratively engineered over the course of the project — the orchestration itself is a second, deliberate piece of engineering alongside the measurement harness and its benchmark, and by now it is interesting in its own right.</p> <p>The full description lives in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> (the loop, the roles, the artifact system, and how the topology itself evolved under its own review machinery); this section is the summary.</p> <p><strong>The division of labor.</strong> Ed sets the research direction, the methodology standards (the decision log&#39;s non-negotiables: raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy headlines, named measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), the hardware and access decisions, and — the part that is easy to underrate — the <em>process policy</em>: every rule below exists because he observed a failure or an opportunity and issued a standing instruction. The AI staff executes: the designated lead agent is the final reviewer and single point of accountability: decomposition, design adjudication, every final diff gate, live verification, merges, and bookkeeping. Independent implementation and review agents do the volume work against pinned specs, adversarial review lenses, test writing, and fresh-instance test auditing; specialist agents handle bounded sweeps. Cross-model review is load-bearing by design: the attributed catch record shows the models and review layers catching different classes of defect.</p> <p><strong>The machinery, briefly.</strong> Independent tasks run as parallel git worktrees, the lead driving each stream&#39;s implementation/review pipeline directly (a topology that is itself the product of a signed cross-model meta-review, then validated by a full session with zero coordination stalls — the evolution is traced in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code>). Every implementation passes through a layered pipeline: a design argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before coding), fresh-instance counterreview lenses with lead-triaged dispositions, a test-amplification round, a writer-never-reviews-its-own-tests audit, the lead&#39;s diff gate, and lead-side live verification on real hardware — the one layer never delegated, because it has repeatedly caught blockers whose own tests were green (the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code). Merges add their own gate: a pre-merge oversight pass by fresh reviewers with distinct angles, and a standing <em>final-head rule</em> — any commit landing after the last review round gets one more fresh review before merge (its first application caught a crash path in a &quot;trivial&quot; late fix). After parallel streams merge, a dedicated integration review hunts the cross-stream defects no per-stream review can see (two interaction defects on its first outing, two more on its second). An event-driven review council convenes for contract-bearing work, and — per Ed&#39;s instruction — its <em>deliberations</em> are recorded, not just its verdicts: the council log preserves positions, the reasoning exchanged, who prevailed and why, and overridden dissents, so a future reader (or model) can reconstruct why any decision was made.</p> <p><strong>The paper trail (each claim traceable to its evidence home; the external re-reduction demonstration is still pending).</strong> Each fact has one home: <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> — the binding design decisions (the log is the count authority), most recording alternatives considered and revisit conditions; <code>docs/council_log.md</code> — the deliberation record; <code>docs/stream_logs/</code> — per-stream decision ledgers committed <em>with</em> the code they justify (wrong decisions are superseded in place, never erased); <code>docs/run_reports/</code> — one record per session with verification evidence, a per-review-layer catch table, and a delegation-calibration ledger (outcomes assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-reported; prompt-defects separated from model-defects). The whole loop is self-instrumenting: every review layer&#39;s unique catches are attributed and tallied, and a layer that stops earning its keep is dropped by its own evidence rule (one already has been). Delegation boundaries move on calibration evidence, not intuition. Lessons are folded into the process playbooks the same session they are learned — measurably: one failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, and zero times after. The loop even reviews itself: a meta-review consensus (C-009) redesigned the coordination topology, and the next session (C-010) validated the redesign with a zero-stall run.</p> <p><strong>What one day of this looks like (2026-07-07).</strong> Five implementation streams plus a repo-wide test audit ran concurrently: statistical uncertainty, contamination detection, deep DVFS telemetry, campaign automation, and a KV-cache size model. All five merged the same day; the test suite grew 254 → 369; the layered review recorded thirteen attributed catches including three blockers that no single reviewer would plausibly have found together. One blocker surfaced only when the real CLI was run against code whose own tests were green, because the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.</p> <p><strong>How the scope grew.</strong> The project began as an architecture sketch for &quot;measure LLM inference energy on edge hardware.&quot; Contracts-first engineering turned that into an auditable instrument: typed configs, self-contained evidence bundles, a strict re-reduction validator. The mock vertical slice proved the math without hardware; the Mac slice produced the first real joules; the flagship run put a 122-billion- parameter mixture-of-experts model through the identical harness and yielded the first real cross-model observation: two confounded points that differ in size, architecture, and quantization, with energy/token behavior consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal model while decode power stays nearly flat — the big model costs time, not watts. This week the instrument gained the statistical and forensic machinery above, and a steelmanned, devil&#39;s-advocated research agenda of 31 tiered questions — 16 answerable on the current hardware alone (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The pattern throughout: capability first, claims only when the instrument can defend them.</p> <p><strong>And the most recent day (2026-07-07/08).</strong> Four checkpointed streams were resumed, completed, and merged in one session: the integrity/ provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed; strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence), the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded ~30 attributed catches, including two blockers no implementer&#39;s tests could see (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation input; a validation-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire contracts overturned by review before they could ever touch hardware, and one fabricated-evidence defect caught only at the lead&#39;s diff gate. The suite went 415 → 546 tests with zero expected failures, and the lead never wrote implementation code and never skipped a gate.</p> <p><strong>Where to look.</strong> <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> is the process description. <code>docs/council_log.md</code> is the deliberation record — C-006 is a full orchestration trace of the five-stream day; C-009/C-010 are the topology meta-review and its validation; C-011 is the critique counter-review. <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> holds the binding design decisions with alternatives considered (the log is the count authority). <code>docs/run_reports/</code> narrates each working session, with per-layer catch tables and the delegation-calibration ledger. The executable orchestration playbooks live outside this repository as reusable skills (council, delegation, multi-stream worktrees, adversarial review, and a top-level operation-loop that sequences them), so the machinery survives this project and transfers to the next one.</p> <h2 id="maintenance-of-this-document">Maintenance Of This Document</h2> <p>Updated at phase transitions and whenever advisor-visible state changes (a gate closes, a verdict lands, the schedule moves). Volatile work-selection facts stay in the state kernel, verification results stay in command/CI output, and decision structure stays in the checked decision-log index. A front-facing change also refreshes <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code>; Ed alone regenerates and deploys the site (D-068).</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>PROJECT_STATUS.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. The arc&#39;s earlier segment (adjudication rounds, PRs #41–#48) is recorded in the CP-5/checkpoint records and stop-card history; this entry records the 2026-07-10/11 continuation.</p> <p>Participants: Fable lead; gpt-5.6-sol as implementer, reviewer, refuter, auditor, and design consultant across ~57 recorded invocations. The lead retained worktree/merge authority, every final diff gate, all live verification, and bookkeeping.</p> <p>Scope of this segment: PR #49 (NV-GATE-2 code-now + flake root-causes) merged <code>1b0f1f6</code> + <code>10e0ad2</code>; PR #54 (P2-041 vetted rebuild from the RED-tranche triage recipe, review + fix round + delta review) merged <code>69a3393</code>; PR #55 (P2-044 idle dependence / HAC / ESS, design-consult-first, review + fix round) merged <code>56d103e</code>. At the Ed-directed pause (stop card checkpoint #4 + amendments) PRs #50–#53 and #56–#58 stood open and lead-gated with the resume order pinned; after resume, the integration tree (<code>c028-integration</code> @ <code>190a0fc</code>, main post-#55 + 7 branches) caught 38 cross-stream failures, the fix round + cross-stream review cleared them, and the full wave merged SHA-guarded (#50, #51, #52, #53, #56, #57, #58 — P2-037 last), with final main verified green and content-identical to the reviewed tree; follow-up PR #59 (from the cross-stream review) is under review and DOC-008 rounds remain in flight. Delegation infrastructure landed on main: adapter, codex-run-v3, usage guard, scope backstop.</p> <p>Closeout amendment (2026-07-11): C-028 is <strong>CLOSED</strong>. PRs #41-#58 are merged; current main&#39;s canonical suite is 1,220 OK (<code>skipped=10</code>) and the corpus gate is 6/6. PR #59 remains open with a 1,224-test green worktree replay (<code>skipped=12</code>), and <code>impl/doc008-kernel</code> is pushed awaiting PR. These open follow-ups do not reopen the card. Every Window-A software gate and P0-003 are satisfied; quiet-machine execution with Ed remains deliberately separate from landed-software status. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability.
